correctness.rationale: The finite input consists of all 210 Petersen induced four-vertex subsets. The supplied self-contained checker reconstructs exactly 140 facets and 766 faces; finds 369 disjoint element-matching pairs with precisely one critical vertex and 26 critical 5-cells; and verifies the entire 765-vertex oriented Hasse graph is acyclic, so discrete Morse gives a wedge of 26 five-spheres. The signed reduced Hopf trace is computed on all 120 group elements, with exact character values and Specht multiplicities. Separate mod-2 chain boundary ranks (9,36,84,126,114) corroborate the topology. No extrapolation beyond this finite graph or equivariant wedge claim is made.

Bayer et al. compute the distinct two-cut Petersen complex, and the sequel studies different graph families; published Petersen total-three-cut and Morse/matching complexes are not this complex. Complete source material for both primary papers was read in pertinent definition, theorem, example and homology-action sections. Residual risk of unindexed equivalent work remains.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is the canonical ten-vertex Kneser graph with full S5 symmetry; a complete higher ordinary cut-complex homotopy classification beyond its published k=2 example is a natural motivated invariant. The result identifies all integral homology by actual homotopy type, plus a nontrivial explicit 26-dimensional rational S5 character and Specht decomposition, data not recoverable from previous nonequivariant two-cut results. It resolves a complete natural finite object rather than an arbitrary parameter slice, routine renaming or known-table recomputation; the exhaustive exact certificate is small and independently replayable.
